instructions: In a large bowl, stir the 2 1/2 cups flour and the salt together. Add 1 cup of water a little at a time, mixing, until you have a soft dough. If it's dry, add a teaspoon of water. If it's sticky, add a spoonful of flour.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured counter for 5 minutes, until smooth. Cover it and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Cut the dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll each one into a round about 8 inches across and 1/4 inch thick, and prick it a few times with a fork.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat and brush it with 1/2 tbsp of the oil. Cook one round for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until both sides are golden and crisp with brown spots. Brush the pan with 1/2 tbsp oil before each of the other rounds.
method_notes: Gurmestan's kita (flour, water, salt, a short rest, a dry pan) and Ethiopian-Food.org's (rounds pricked with a fork and cooked in a little fat until crisp and spotted) agree on the dough. Ratios differ: Gurmestan uses about 3/8 cup water per cup of flour, Ethiopian-Food.org about 4/7; this uses 2/5. Both fry in niter kibbeh (clarified butter), which is swapped for vegetable oil so it stays vegan and dairy-free. Neither source shows a rating, so this counts as a fallback.
